Definition: from G575 and κρίνω; to conclude for oneself, i.e. (by implication) to respond; by Hebraism (compare H6030) to begin to speak (where an address is expected):--answer.
BiblicalUsage: To answer — the commonest verb of reply in the Gospels, two hundred and thirty-two times. Jesus answers John the Baptist at His baptism in Matthew 3:15, ‘thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness,’ and John answers the priests in John 1:26, ‘I baptize with water: but there standeth one among you, whom ye know not.’ Before Pilate in Luke 23:3 Jesus answers, ‘Thou sayest it,’ and in John 19:11 He answers that Pilate could have no power at all against Him except it were given from above.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word shows me that answering is itself a kind of witness. Jesus answers with a sentence that fulfils righteousness, and with a sentence that gives power back to God, and sometimes He answers with two words and lets them stand. The wisdom is knowing when a word will fulfil righteousness and when silence will.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; John the Baptist; Pontius Pilate
